_comment: Email content for the latest release. Update this each release as part of /release-update, then run send.mjs. Keep it to the highlights; this is an email, not the full changelog. British English, no em dashes, no emojis, no permanence words.
subject: InnerZero 0.2.1 is out
preheader: A newer Ollama runtime, feedback with an optional redacted log, Zero can explain the app, and network Ollama for low-spec machines.
intro: Version 0.2.1 of InnerZero is now available. It updates the bundled AI runtime, makes it easier to send us useful feedback, and opens the door for machines that cannot run a model of their own. Here are the highlights.

groups.label: New
items: Attach your app log to feedback: the sidebar feedback box can include the last 15 minutes, hour, or day of InnerZero's activity log, reduced to event names, labels, and sizes only, with a preview before anything is sent.
Ask Zero about InnerZero itself: questions like how do I change the theme or what can you do are answered from a built-in guide to the app.
Use an Ollama server on your network from a low-spec machine: point Settings > AI & Models at another computer running Ollama and chat works from there without a local model.

groups.label: Improved
items: Bundled Ollama updated from 0.22 to 0.32, with Vulkan GPU acceleration on by default for AMD and Intel GPUs. NVIDIA GPUs need driver 550 or newer for GPU acceleration (570 or newer for older Maxwell and Pascal cards).

Office documents such as .pptx and .docx are recognised as files in chat, Settings > Hardware names every GPU it detects, and 32 GB machines that report slightly less usable RAM now land on the right tier.
Connecting a network Ollama server no longer suggests a pointless restart, and the model list refreshes from the new server straight away.

groups.label: Fixed
items: A No Local Model machine no longer answers hi and then blocks every real question.
Updating on Windows now removes the previous version's AI runtime libraries instead of leaving them behind.
Deleting a calendar event that was pushed to Google keeps its link to the Google copy until you confirm.
